sn12.23:1.2: The “ending of defilements” (_āsavānaṁ khayaṁ_) is a common sutta term for arahantship. | “Knowing and seeing” refers to the penetrating insight that arises from meditative immersion (_samādhi_, eg. [an5.168:2.2](), [an10.2:2.3](), [sn12.23:6.18](), [dn2:83.1]()). | The opening is the same as [sn22.101]() and [sn22.101]().
sn12.23:2.1: An _upanisā_ is a conditional factor that is both necessary and strongly conducive. It functions in Pali as an contraction of _upanissaya_ (“depend on”). Elsewhere, _saupanisa_ is used of the seven path factors as “vital conditions” for right immersion ([sn45.28:1.2](), [mn117:2.1]()). | It is not clear if _upanisā_ is the same as the Sanskrit _upaniṣad_, for which the oldest sense is “correspondence, equivalence”, referring to the secret links between things (Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 10.4.5.1; Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 3.9.26, 4.2.1; Chāndogya Upaniṣad 3.11.3, 8.8.4; Taittirīya Upaniṣad 1.11.4, 2.9.1). These equivalences are explained in the esoteric teachings that themselves came to be known as Upaniṣads. Pali _upanisā_ is also found in the unrelated sense “sitting close” to a teacher ([an3.67:6.7]()).
sn12.23:2.3: “Freedom” here is the liberation from defilements, namely arahantship itself. The arahant reviews their freedom, which is the “knowledge of ending”.
